newsitem.title: GERMANY: Yeltsin illness known before June poll - former aide.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin illness known before June poll - former aide.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin was too ill to work properly weeks before the first round of the presidential election last June, his former chief bodyguard and confidant said in an interview with the weekly Der Spiegel.

Other Moscow officials have so far insisted that Yeltsin, now preparing for a multiple heart bypass operation later this year, was in good health before the first round of the election on June 16, but that his heart condition worsened days later.

However Alexander Korzhakov, a long-time Yeltsin confidant and eminence grise who was sacked in a purge of Kremlin hawks before the second round of the election in early July, said he and others feared for Yeltsin's health in May.
At the time, Korzhakov even called for the entire election to be postponed and said Yeltsin, who had put himself through a punishing vote-gathering campaign, could stay in office without a poll.
"We could see clearly how exhausted Yeltsin was and that he might not survive a demanding election campaign," Korzhakov told the magazine, according to an advance release from Monday's edition.
"The doctors who were treating him told me in writing as early as May 20 about the danger. Their warning sounded dramatic: The president can only work for a few hours a day," Korzhakov said.
Asked why he had never made this letter public, Korzhakov accused Yeltsin's daughter Tatyana of controlling the flow of information to the president.
"At that time my influence on the president was already reduced," he said.

"(Yelstin) returned from a state visit to Paris with the brilliant idea that daughters are the ideal campaign managers for their president-fathers...Since then (Tatyana) alone supplies her father with information -- or what she considers appropriate."
